records.name: Tallowmere
records.description: Major walled port on the northwestern shore of the central inland sea, built around a sheltered natural harbor where a navigable river reaches the sea. Governed locally by House Denvor under a hereditary charter confirmed by House Kharadorn.

records.name: Millhaven
records.description: Grain village and mill center on the River Vale, about 9 miles northwest of Tallowmere. Principal grain collection point supplying the city.

records.name: Brackenholt
records.description: Woodland and charcoal settlement west of Tallowmere within the Brackenwood, serving timber, charcoal, and managed woodland trades.

records.name: Stonehollow
records.description: Quarry settlement southwest of Tallowmere in the Greyback Ridges, supplying worked stone and quarry labor.

records.name: Ashcombe Manor
records.description: Agricultural estate on Ashcombe Rise overlooking the Northfields and northern road.

records.name: Fordmere
records.description: Upriver settlement at a dependable crossing of the River Vale, with a chartered crossing administered by House Merewick and a ferry supplement.

records.name: Saltwick
records.description: Working shore settlement southeast of Tallowmere with fishing, salt-working, and a modest beacon.

records.name: Harthbridge
records.description: Town on the South Road, about 27 miles from Tallowmere, governed under House Velleran's town charter and outside direct Denvor administration.

records.name: River Vale
records.description: Principal inland route serving Tallowmere, descending from the western uplands through the farm country and into the harbor.

records.name: Brackenwood
records.description: Worked woodland west of Tallowmere supplying fuel, poles, timber, game, and gathered plants.

records.name: Greyback Ridges
records.description: Stony hills southwest of Tallowmere, with Stonehollow quarries on accessible eastern faces.

records.name: Northfields
records.description: Open agricultural country north and northeast of Tallowmere with farms, orchards, pasture, hedgerows, and drainage hollows.

records.name: Eastern Shore
records.description: Irregular shore southeast of Tallowmere with low bluffs, coves, beaches, fishing landings, and salt-working places.

records.name: Old Stone Bridge
records.description: Principal permanent river crossing within Tallowmere.

records.name: Bellwater Pool
records.description: Deep, slow pool on the River Vale upstream of Millhaven, used by bargemen as a waiting and turning place.

records.name: Saltwick Beacon
records.description: Modest shore beacon maintained by Saltwick boat-owning households as a navigation and storm-warning aid.

records.name: Greywatch Rise
records.description: Elevated heart of noble authority containing House Denvor's fortified residence, principal garrison buildings, formal gardens, and senior household residences.

records.name: The High Ward
records.description: Older, wealthier residential quarter with townhouses, legal offices, established temples, private courtyards, and prosperous families.

records.name: The Old Quays
records.description: Old working waterfront with stone warehouses, chandlers, shipwrights, rope-makers, taverns, and established shipping offices.

records.name: The New Quays
records.description: Expanded wharves and storage yards serving larger vessels, bulk cargo, bonded warehouses, and newer merchant concerns.

records.name: Market Ward
records.description: Commercial center with principal market square, guildhalls, moneychangers, inns, public notices, and specialist shops.

records.name: Rivergate
records.description: River-facing district of bargemen, millers, fishmongers, carters, small foundries, tanners, and laborers.

records.name: Lantern Ward
records.description: District of shrines, temples, charitable houses, healers, burial grounds, and religious hostels.

records.name: The Underways
records.description: Umbrella surface term for accessible subterranean spaces and routes beneath Tallowmere where ratfolk communities live and work. Not one unified settlement or faction.
